question:
Two narrow monochromatic light sources $S_1$ and $S_2$ illuminate a screen and their waves superpose at a point $P$. Source $S_1$ emits with angular frequency $\omega$ and source $S_2$ emits with angular frequency $\omega+\Delta\omega$, where $\Delta\omega$ is small but non-zero.

A student claims: “Since the frequencies are different, interference can never be observed.”

Evaluate this claim by discussing what happens to the interference term in the intensity when

(i) the observation time is very short compared to $\dfrac{2\pi}{\Delta\omega}$.

(ii) the detector or eye averages the intensity over a time much longer than $\dfrac{2\pi}{\Delta\omega}$.

Conclude whether the student’s statement is correct or incorrect.

options.A: The student is correct: different frequencies always give uniform intensity at all times, so interference never occurs.
options.B: The student is incorrect: interference exists, but the phase difference changes with time so the fringe pattern is not stationary; for long time averaging the interference term averages to zero.
options.C: The student is incorrect: a stable stationary interference pattern always forms, but the fringe width changes with time.
options.D: The student is correct: coherence is possible only if $\Delta\omega=0$ at every instant, so no interference can be observed for $\Delta\omega\neq 0$.
